newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schenker to manage BASF distribution centre.
newsitem.headline: Schenker to manage BASF distribution centre.

text.p: Schenker-Rhenus AG said it has taken over management of the Scandinavia distribution terminal of German chemicals giant BASF.
The BASF regional distribution centre in Copenhagen has been run by its Danish subsidiary, Schenker-Albert Nielsen A/S, since the start of the year, a Schenker statement said.
Some 30,000 tonnes of chemical products are distributed a year from the 5,000 square metre centre which holds about 5,000 tonnes at any one time, the statement added.

Schenker Eurocargo, the Schenker-Rhenus road and railfreight subsidiary, organises rail transport from the BASF headquarters in Ludwigshafen to Copenhagen and daily distribution throughout Scandinavia.
It is also responsible for staffing and building management under the logistics contract.
Data and information is exchanged through a direct link between the Schenker and BASF communications systems.
The new BASF centre, the first of several planned European regional terminals, is designed to shorten delivery times significantly.
